subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Healthy habits: 60 minutes a day, sleep and rest
objectives: State the daily activity guideline for young people
Explain why sleep and recovery matter
Plan a healthy week of activity

keywords.def: exercise that makes you warm and breathe faster, but you can still talk
exercise that makes you breathe hard and you can say only a few words
time for the body to rest and repair

starter: Bismillah. Name three components of fitness.
How do you find your pulse?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Listen to your body and rest when needed
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: How much activity?
bullets: UK guidance: an average of 60 minutes a day
teach.note: The UK Chief Medical Officers advise children and young people aged 5 to 18 to average at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity a day across the week. Ask what counts: walking to the masjid, playing, skipping.

teach.heading: Moderate or vigorous?
bullets: Moderate: you breathe faster but can still talk
Vigorous: you can only say a few words
teach.note: Do the talk test: pupils jog gently and say a sentence; then faster.

teach.heading: Sleep and recovery
bullets: Good sleep helps learning and mood
Rest days are part of training
teach.note: Link to the hadith that your body has a right over you (Sahih al-Bukhari): rest is also a right. Misconception: more exercise is always better.

teach.heading: Plan a week
bullets: Include a rest or gentle day
teach.note: Pupils fill in a weekly planner with realistic activities that need no equipment.

practice: Give an example of moderate activity.
independent: Sort ten activities into moderate or vigorous.
Do a talk test while jogging on the spot.
exit: Plan your own week of 60 minutes a day with rest included.
Write two reasons why sleep helps your fitness.
homework: How much activity do experts advise for young people?
lessons.send: Follow your plan for three days and tick each activity.

lessons.title: Building stamina with intervals
objectives: Rate effort on a 1 to 10 scale

keywords.def: ability to keep going for a long time
a short burst of work followed by rest
how hard it feels you are working

starter: What is the daily activity guideline?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Stop if you feel sick or faint
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: What is an interval?
bullets: A work period then a rest period
teach.note: Explain intervals as the pattern of a hard push and a recovery. Misconception: intervals mean going flat out.

teach.heading: Effort scale 1 to 10
teach.note: Teach pupils to rate their effort. Aim for 6 to 7 during intervals.

teach.heading: Interval session
teach.note: Use a visible clock. Coach pace not speed. Include a warm-up and cool-down.

teach.heading: Reflect
teach.note: Ask for effort ratings after each block. Encourage perseverance (sabr).

independent: Do a 3-minute warm-up and rate your effort.
Do three intervals of 30 seconds work and 30 seconds rest.
exit: Complete six intervals and note your effort rating after each.
Write one thing you can do to improve next time.
homework: What is the benefit of interval training?
Rate effort of a gentle walk.
lessons.send: Repeat the session with a family member on two days.
